subject: Aurora - Dedicated GPU footprint and scaling scenarios
messages:
From: Luke Harper <luke.harper@aurorahealth.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-01 16:41:00 +0000
Subject: Aurora workload sketch + SLO targets (early)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking the time yesterday. I wanted to capture the high-level workload we discussed so your team can start a sizing sketch. High-level constraints:
- Product: real-time summarization + follow-up Q&A embedded in our clinician UI. Typical session: initial 400-800 token note + 1-3 short follow-ups (~40-80 tokens).
- Expected launch month 2028-01; early adoption cohort = 2k DAUs, target GA 50k DAUs.
- Expected requests/day (GA target): ~1.2M requests/day. Avg tokens/request ~180.
- Latency SLO (p95): <= 350ms generation latency per request (we can stream, but p95 end-to-end should be under 350ms).
- Peak traffic profile: 4x average during clinical hours (08:00-18:00 local).

Questions for sizing: what dedicated GPU commit would you recommend for the GA target to hit the p95 latency SLO with ~20% headroom for spikes? Also want to understand cost delta between a conservative (30% headroom) and lean (10% headroom) commit.

I've attached a simple workload spreadsheet and our procurement timeline. Happy to jump on a quick scoping call.

Best,
Luke Harper
Head of Product, Aurora Healthtech

Attachments: aurora_workload_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), procurement_timeline.pdf (brief)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Luke Harper <luke.harper@aurorahealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-01 20:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Aurora workload sketch + SLO targets (early)

Luke — thanks, this is really helpful. Quick read of the numbers and a few clarifying Qs below, plus a first-pass commitment estimate.

Clarifying Qs:
- Model family: are you planning to run an MPT-style 70B or a smaller 13/30B family for latency-first inference? (This changes per-GPU token throughput a lot.)
- Max seq length we should budget for (prompt+response): you listed ~800 for the initial note; is 1,024 a safe ceiling?
- Any regulatory constraint requiring on-prem or strict VPC-only?

First-pass assumptions I used (based on similar health workloads):
- GA workload: 1.2M req/day * 180 tokens = 216M tokens/day average.
- Average tokens/sec (24h): 216M / 86,400 ≈ 2,500 tokens/sec.
- Peak window (clinical hours, 4x average): peak tokens/sec ≈ 10,000 tokens/sec.
- Model: latency-optimized 13B quantized variant with per-GPU sustained throughput ≈ 12,000 tokens/sec at p95 for streaming generation at the target seq lengths.

Sizing math (simple):
- Raw GPUs = ceil(peak_tokens_sec / per_gpu_tps) = ceil(10,000 / 12,000) = 1 GPU (mathically), but we do not run production with single-GPU headroom.
- Apply headroom factor: for 20% headroom need capacity for 12,000 tokens/sec => ceil(12,000 / 12,000) = 1; for 30% headroom => 13,000 tokens/sec => still 2? wait — because single physical GPU may saturate other operational dimensions (concurrency, KV cache, failover).

Operational considerations that push GPU count up:
- Redundancy (N+1) for node failover: recommend at least two nodes for high availability.
- Model variants/fallbacks: we recommend reserving capacity for a quantized fallback or larger-context flows (e.g., longer transcripts).
- Autoscaling burst capacity limits on Dedicated: short bursts above committed capacity can be handled, but with cost spikes.

Initial recommended proposals: 
1) Conservative (30% headroom, N+1 HA): commit 4 GPUs (2 primary + 1 failover + 1 buffer for bursts/variant).
2) Balanced (20% headroom): commit 3 GPUs (2 primary + 1 failover).
3) Lean (10% headroom, early GA w/ aggressive autoscale): commit 2 GPUs (1 primary + 1 failover) and allow burst to hosted pool for rare spikes.

Cost delta and exact throughput per GPU depend on the final model family and quantization profile; I can run a micro-benchmark on our infra if you can confirm target model family.

Next steps: I’ll loop in Marissa and Rishi to translate this into a short SLA/cost table + rollout timeline and attach a more detailed math sheet. Can we set a 30-min follow-up Tue 11/02?

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-01 21:10:00 +0000
Subject: FW: Aurora workload sketch + SLO targets (early) — sizing inputs + ask

Team — forwarding Luke's sketch. I did a quick first-pass (copied into the attached spreadsheet). Wanted your input on the following and a crisp recommendation we can present tomorrow: 

Requirements recap (GA target):
- 1.2M req/day, 180 tokens/req avg => 216M tokens/day.
- Peak tokens/sec ~10k (4x diurnal). p95 latency target <= 350ms.
- Must plan for HA and procure ahead of Jan 2028 GA.

Micro-benchmark assumptions used here: 13B quantized (vRedwood-13q), steady-state per-GPU = 12k tokens/sec at p95; cold-start and longer-context flows (>=1024 tokens) reduce sustained throughput ~25%.

Detailed options with raw math (see attached spreadsheet):
- Option A (Conservative): 4 GPUs commit
  - Calculations: baseline capacity (2 GPUs primary) => 24k tps capacity; after N+1 and variant reserve, commit 4 GPUs.
  - Headroom: ~120% on peak; supports longer-context overflow and maintenance windows.

- Option B (Balanced): 3 GPUs commit
  - Baseline primary: 2 GPUs (24k tps), 1 additional for failover and modest burst.
  - Headroom ~60-80% on peak depending on model mix.

- Option C (Lean + burst to hosted): 2 GPUs commit + hosted bursting
  - Lower committed spend; risk is procurement/throughput alignment and potential throttling during multi-hour surges.

Questions for you all:
1) For procurement timeline we need an ops SLA option: can we present 99.95% availability with N+1 and a 4-GPU commit? Marissa, can you sketch the SLA/cost delta?
2) Rishi — for long-context fallback: how much effective throughput drop should we budget when we estimate mixed traffic (20% of requests use >1024 tokens)? I used 25% above but want your sanity check.
3) Monica — if Aurora wants regionally colocated nodes (east/central/us-west) do we recommend a single region first then replicate at 6-9 months? Any procurement constraints?

Attachments included for the call: aurora_workload_v1.xlsx, aurora_rollout_map.pdf, aurora_procurement_requirements.docx

Thanks — if you can each drop quick bullets I’ll consolidate into a 1-pager for Luke.

—Karthik
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-02 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: FW: Aurora workload sketch + SLO targets (early) — sizing inputs + ask

Quick bullets for the 1-pager (ops / procurement view):
- SLA: 99.95% with N+1 across the committed pool. For 3-GPU commit we offer best-effort failover and 99.9% SLA; 4-GPU commit required for 99.95% guarantee.
- Cost delta (ballpark, monthly committed GPU-equivalent):
  - 2 GPUs: $Xk/month (lean) – lower fixed cost, higher burst exposure to hosted pricing.
  - 3 GPUs: $Yk/month (balanced).
  - 4 GPUs: $Zk/month (conservative) – includes buffer for maintenance and regional replication runway.
- Recommendation: present Balanced (3 GPUs) and Conservative (4 GPUs) options to Aurora. Emphasize that 3→4 is an easy one-time expansion if early GA grows faster than forecast.
- Procurement checklist: SOC2 evidence, KMS integration timeline, ingress/egress IP allowlist, and PO terms (we need 30-day net standard unless procurement requests longer).

Rishi — on throughput drop for long-context: I concur with Karthik's 25% degradation for the 13B quantized path; if Aurora selects a 30B family, plan for 45-50% throughput drop.

Monica — on regional replica timing: recommend single-region GA (US-East) with pre-approved replication playbook; replicate to US-West by Q2 post-GA if utilisation >70% sustained.

I’ll draft the 1-pager and cost table now and attach.

—Marissa
Director, Solutions Ops

Subject: Re: Aurora workload sketch + SLO targets (early) — recommended next steps

Luke — attaching the 1-pager and the detailed workbook we used to produce the three commitment options. TL;DR recommendation is to present Aurora with two commercial options:

1) Balanced: 3 GPUs committed (2 primary + 1 failover) — expected to meet p95 <= 350ms for the 13B quantized profile with ~60-80% headroom on peak; lower up-front spend and straightforward procurement.
2) Conservative: 4 GPUs committed (N+1 plus buffer) — recommended if Aurora requires the 99.95% SLA and wants room for longer-context fallbacks without bursting.

We propose the following next steps:
- Confirm model family (13B quantized preferred for latency). If Aurora confirms, we run a 24-hour micro-benchmark within 48 hours to validate per-GPU sustained tps numbers and refine the cost table.
- Kick off procurement: I’ve looped procurement@aurorahealth.ai; Marissa attached the SLA/cost table and procurement checklist.
- Schedule scoping call w/ engineering to lock region and rollout phasing — what does Tue 11/09 14:00 ET look like?

Deliverables attached: aurora_1pager_commit_options.pdf, aurora_workload_v1.xlsx, aurora_rollout_map.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk through the math.

—Karthik
